claims.text: High-temperature plastic strain and toughness in fusion plasma-facing alloys are governed by the formation and stability of uniformly distributed, fine, coherent nanoprecipitates.
A controlled annealing or aging sequence can induce stable, coherent nanoprecipitates in the alloy matrix.
Fine nanoprecipitates impede dislocation glide and thereby strengthen the alloy.
Coherent precipitate interfaces permit controlled dislocation transmission.
Precipitate-mediated controlled slip delays localized plastic instability.
Stable, coherent nanoprecipitates delay crack initiation.
Stable nanoprecipitates enhance high-temperature strength and yield behavior.
Alloys without engineered nanoprecipitates undergo precipitate coarsening or dissolution at high temperature.
Precipitate coarsening or dissolution increases dislocation mobility.
Increased dislocation mobility caused by precipitate coarsening or dissolution produces higher high-temperature plastic strain rates.
Thermally processed material containing coherent nanoprecipitates will have a statistically significant lower high-temperature plastic strain rate than the unprocessed baseline.
Thermally processed material containing coherent nanoprecipitates will have greater toughness, including higher fracture toughness, than the unprocessed baseline.
The unprocessed baseline naturally tends toward precipitate coarsening or dissolution during high-temperature service.
The unprocessed baseline consequently exhibits higher plastic strain rates and lower toughness.
Mechanical testing at 600–1000 °C can represent fusion plasma-facing operating conditions for the proposed alloy comparison.
The proposed mechanism applies when dislocation motion, rather than extensive grain-boundary sliding, dominates deformation.
The magnitude of nanoprecipitate-related mechanical improvements varies with alloy composition and processing conditions.
High-temperature deformation mechanisms other than nanoprecipitate-controlled dislocation motion may contribute outside the stated conditions.
